constraints: The Git provider requires Node filesystem APIs.
JSON is the only supported Git content format.
Generic Git singleton content is read from singletons/<key>.json through the provider-neutral getSingleton operation.
Dedicated navigation and settings content are read from navigation/<key>.json and settings/<key>.json through their dedicated provider operations.
Locale-aware retrieval resolves variants from <directory>/<locale>/<file>.json with a fallback chain when locales are configured; the legacy flat path is preserved when they are not.
The WordPress provider is read-only, retrieves published content, and requires a complete WordPress REST API v2 root.
No synchronization, webhook, or preview workflow is implemented.
Localisation covers locale configuration, fallback resolution, and Git variant directories; translation workflows are not implemented.
SEO canonical URLs are supplied by content or consumers; Core does not infer deployment URLs.
The package remains private while the pre-1.0 architecture is proven.

The repaired pre-release WordPress companion contract uses version 1 envelopes with data and optional diagnostics, three editor modes, 12 canonical short section names, and five nexuscontent/v1 route contracts.
The companion plugin remains in progress until its WordPress integration suite passes in CI; local Docker, MySQL, SVN, and WP-CLI are unavailable.
Released 0.2.0 standard WordPress REST provider retrieval remains unchanged and does not call the companion plugin.
architecturalDecisions: Providers do not depend on frontend frameworks.
Consumers own routes, presentation, page composition, and framework integration.
Git-based CMS products use the Git provider when repository files are authoritative.
Provider-specific response structures stop at the provider boundary.
Ordinary content retrieval does not perform Git synchronization.
Astro is a reference consumer, not a Core dependency.
Generic singleton content remains available for arbitrary singleton data, while navigation and settings use dedicated APIs, types, configuration sections, and Git directories.
Multiple instances of the same provider type must remain possible.
Locale resolution is centralized in Core; providers implement variant file resolution; format adapters and validators implement no locale logic.
Locale requests fall back through an explicit chain to the configured default; projects without locale configuration keep the legacy flat retrieval path unchanged.
Core owns normalized SEO data, validation, and deterministic resolution; providers map source data and consumers own metadata rendering.
The WordPress companion plugin is isolated under integrations/wordpress/nexuscontent and does not change Core or released standard REST provider retrieval.
Phase 3 provider integration must consume only the repaired contract after companion plugin integration verification passes.
